claims.value: Diplomatic relations with the United States

scope.description: Explicit historical institution, office, affiliation or event of the named entity; not an inference about polygon sovereignty or statistical territory.

evidence.note: The official history dates diplomatic relations to 1862 and states that strong ties continued into the 1990s; this record is restricted to the atlas framework.

qualifications: Diplomatic relationship, not United States sovereignty over Liberia.
No assertion of identical diplomatic staffing, financial support or agreement throughout the interval.
Coarse research endpoint years remain partial; earlier or later events are not back-projected.

claims.value: An international commission submitted its report on slavery and forced labour to the Liberian government.

scope.description: Explicit historical institution, office, affiliation or event of the named entity; not an inference about polygon sovereignty or statistical territory.

evidence.note: The contemporary memorandum explicitly dates submission to 8 September 1930.

qualifications: The commission included American, League of Nations-nominated and Liberian members. Findings are attributed to the commission; submission is not evidence that the abuses immediately ceased.

claims.value: The Liberian president notified the United States that the government accepted the international commission’s recommendations.

scope.description: Explicit historical institution, office, affiliation or event of the named entity; not an inference about polygon sovereignty or statistical territory.

evidence.note: The memorandum records the notification on 30 September and distinguishes promises from implemented reforms.

qualifications: The same memorandum reports that definite implementation plans had not yet been received. Acceptance must not be represented as completed abolition or implementation.
